nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression normative modeling implemented with PCNtoolkit (v0.28).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To implement normative modeling, we utilized the PCNtoolkit Python package, version 0.28 (Rutherford et al., 2022). To minimize the impact of site-related variability on subsequent results, hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was employed in the HC cohort to develop a normative model of network degree centrality as a function of age and sex for each brain region (Fig. 1B).

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Degree centrality (AUC across sparsity thresholds 0.05-0.50) of 96 brain regions (Harvard-Oxford atlas).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Degree centrality for each brain region was calculated at every sparsity threshold... with the area under the curve (AUC) across all thresholds defined as a summarized scalar of network indicators... Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was employed in the HC cohort to develop a normative model of network degree centrality

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Normative model of degree centrality as a function of age and sex with site-specific effects via HBR.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: In this study, age and sex were mapped onto the degree centrality of brain functional networks. HBR allows for the imposition of a common prior distribution across multiple sites to estimate site-specific yet interrelated means and variances, thus accommodating signal and noise variability in multisite data while preserving meaningful site-related variations (Bayer et al., 2022; Kia et al., 2020).
